rationale: C05 is a clear drafting precursor. Both are memoranda to executive department and agency heads concerning Federal-service voluntary fundraising under the newly approved policy. They use the same operative sequence: describe the charitable campaign, identify its timing and relationship to the new fundraising policy, appoint named campaign leadership, and urge Federal personnel to support that leadership. The child's campaign for National Health Agencies is also expressly connected to the campaign structure introduced in C05. C21 is next strongest because it combines national health-agency fundraising, a defined campaign period, Federal cooperation, and an appeal to employees, but its administrative structure is less closely matched. C10 shares the chairman-designation and support formula but concerns the older Red Cross campaign framework.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Campaign will be conducted during the six-weeks period beginning February 25, 1957, concurrently with the campaign for CARE and Crusade for Freedom under the new fund-raising policy approved June 27, 1956.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is also the first of two campaigns in the Greater Washington Metropolitan Area to be conducted in Federal offices under the new approved Federal service fund-raising policy.
shared_material.explanation: Both situate a particular charitable campaign within the same newly approved Federal-service fundraising policy and coordinated campaign system.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Sherman Adams has kindly consented to serve as Chairman ... He will be assisted by Arthur Larson and Maurice Stans as Associate Chairmen.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I appoint the Honorable James P. Mitchell, Secretary of Labor, to act as Chairman of the 1956 Government Unit
shared_material.explanation: The later memorandum reuses the concrete machinery of naming campaign leadership for a Federal-service charitable appeal.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I urge that everyone give the Chairman and Associate Chairmen his full support in this important and worthy endeavor.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I urge that everyone give the Chairman his full measure of support in this worthy effort.
shared_material.explanation: This is highly similar concluding language performing the same operative function, with only the plural leadership and final noun changed.
